transcript: I have been following the development of Bliss since it had first had its world premiere production at the Fifth Avenue Theater in Seattle. They released an EP of, like, five songs. Every single one of them is a banger. So when it was announced that it was going to be performing at fringe, obviously I had to go. And this is so interesting to me because Bliss is a you act musical that they've cut down to 80 minutes to perform here at the fringe. And you can tell this feels like a very truncated version. Scenes are chopped up, there's a clear song that feels like the end of act one. But obviously this is a one act musical and so the show keeps going. It makes it very clunky, which is unfortunate because I think the material at the core here, especially these songs, are really, really good. But I don't know if this is the best way to perform it. In addition to that, the overall design felt very mechanical in a way that did not suit the material to me. It reminded me of once upon a one more time, and not in a good way, because I feel like the design for Bliss could be really magical, and it's just not giving that at all right now. But again, there's only so much you can do at fringe. I think that there's really good material in here and a fairy tale that showcases these Princesses that are locked away and protected by their overprotective father. And the kind of optimism that that gives them, so that when they get into the real world and start experiencing the cruelty of the real world, how they deal with that challenge and then sort of move on together from it. Look, I think the story at its core is really well done. If they just had the time that it feels like they usually have to expand on this story. There's something here. I don't necessarily know if giving us a truncated version at the fringe was the right way to showcase it, but I cannot wait to see a full production of Bliss in the future. If you are at fringe and do want to go see this, I think the performances are fantastic. Just know you're getting the Cliffnotes version of Bliss here, not the full version. Go in expecting that. It feels very clunky at times because of how much they've cut in this. If you are not able to see it, though, or want to free up some space, then I definitely at least recommend listening to these tracks. They've released five of the songs that are all really great. There's potential here, just maybe not in this format.
